PullRequest.Title: Fix blocked sessions CI indication when agent merge is enabled
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request updates the Blocked Sessions feature to align its behavior with other session indicators regarding CI failure notifications when Agent Merge is enabled. 

Changes include:

- Blocked Sessions will now hide CI failure indications if Agent Merge is enabled and the "Fix CI" action is also enabled.
- The implementation ensures that sessions requiring input or approval remain visible.
- The changes react appropriately to global settings and per-session overrides.
- CI warnings will still be preserved for sessions not managed by Agent Merge.

Validation was successful with 37 tests passing, along with lint and layer/type checks.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed dependency, always-live non-stable consumers, provider observation hook, wire-level subscribe, snapshot response, per-session maps, and idle-release guard are all directly traced in repository code and supported by the provider test asserting one session subscribe while observed and one unsubscribe only after observer disposal plus 31 seconds. Only real-world F and snapshot size are unknown.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Per-session agent-host wire subscriptions, full SessionState snapshots, and server/client retained session-state objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost grows linearly with the number F of unarchived, non-running agent-host sessions whose open PR currently has failing CI; the loop starts all F asynchronous subscriptions without a limiter, and each remains retained while the failed-CI condition is observed.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: An IPC/network burst and avoidable client/agent-host memory retention during restored-workbench blocked-session computation, with higher startup/background load for users with many failed sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The blocked-session scan only used shared GitHub PR/CI model references and did not acquire agent-host session-state subscriptions. Those subscriptions were otherwise scoped to active/visible Agent Merge UI consumers and released after their observers left.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Reading the Agent Merge configuration in the all-sessions blocked scan observes each matching provider state observable. In BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider, first observation calls _keepAgentMergeSessionStateAlive, which acquires a StateComponents.Session subscription and applies the returned full state snapshot.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT line 148 is the first dependency from the global blocked-session computation to the per-session Agent Merge state observable; production observation of that observable is what acquires and pins the wire subscription.
Findings.Title: Avoid subscribing every failed session to full agent-host state
Findings.Impact: In non-stable builds the application badge and blocked indicator are long-lived consumers. Restoring a workspace with F historical unarchived failed-CI sessions now sends F concurrent subscribe requests and keeps all F session states pinned instead of allowing the provider's 30-second idle release and host cache eviction; remote-agent users also pay the snapshot transfer. Typical F and snapshot sizes are uncertain, so severity is medium, but the fan-out and lifetime are explicit in the call path.
Findings.Evidence: BlockedSessions iterates the complete deduplicated sessions list and line 148 newly observes getSessionAgentMergeConfigurationObservable after a CI failure. That helper reads BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider.getAgentMergeClientStateObservable; its observed event calls _keepAgentMergeSessionStateAlive, which invokes connection.getSubscription(StateComponents.Session, backendUri, ...). AgentSubscriptionManager immediately launches _subscribe(resource), and the protocol server returns the session snapshot. The provider records observed IDs in a set and only schedules its 30-second unsubscribe when the last observer is removed, so the always-live blocked scan prevents idle release. Existing reference maps coalesce multiple BlockedSessions consumers to one wire subscription per session, but do not coalesce across sessions.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not read the subscription-owning per-session observable from the global scan. Supply the blocked-session model with a provider-level batched Agent Merge summary/cache (or otherwise coalesce state loading at provider scope) so off-screen sessions can be classified without pinning one full session subscription each; preserve reactive updates while ensuring subscriptions are bounded and released.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restored-workbench blocked indicators and application badge classify all unarchived sessions with failing CI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The long-lived non-stable title-bar indicator and default-enabled application badge synchronously scan the merged session list. Initial rendering does not await agent-host snapshots, but authoritative Agent Merge suppression depends on the asynchronously returned per-session snapshots; the resulting transport and restoration work runs concurrently with post-restore UI work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to StateComponents.Session and transfer a full session-state snapshot from the local or remote agent host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cold wire subscribe and snapshot per distinct matching backend session, up to F; existing active references coalesce only the same resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: BlockedSessions acquired only local shared GitHub model references. Agent-host session-state subscriptions were acquired by active/visible Agent Merge UI consumers, not by the global failed-CI scan.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited for the first badge paint, but required for authoritative blocked-state classification and initiated as an unbounded post-restore burst; retained subscriptions continue forwarding state updates and pin host/client state.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F deduplicated, unarchived, non-InProgress agent-host sessions with open non-draft pull requests whose already-loaded CI status is Failure; F can include off-screen historical sessions and is not viewport-bounded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The scan invokes each cold session observable synchronously. AgentSubscriptionManager launches one asynchronous subscribe per distinct backend session with no shared limiter, so effective concurrency is F. Provider/session caches coalesce duplicate consumers and existing subscriptions for the same session, but not different sessions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PR and CI references are shared by repository/PR/head and preserved across recomputes with delayedStore; this diff does not add GitHub fetches. Agent Merge configuration is WeakMap-cached per ISession and provider state observables are Map-cached per session. A cold failed session creates one wire subscription; warm reads share it. Because the blocked scan remains an observer while CI fails, the provider's 30-second idle-release timer never starts, so there is no eviction until the dependency disappears, the session is removed, or the owning contribution is disposed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added observable read directly reaches the production observation hook, subscription manager, protocol subscribe, snapshot response, and idle-release guard; repository tests verify subscribe-on-observe and delayed unsubscribe.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The distribution of F, full SessionState snapshot sizes, and remote-agent latency is not measured. The per-session wire request, snapshot, unbounded aggregate concurrency, and retained lifetime are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out and cache-lifecycle regression: the diff turns global failed-CI classification into F concurrent full-state subscriptions and pins off-screen session state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Runtime CI transitions, per-session Agent Merge toggles, and global Agent Merge setting changes update blocked status
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A CI transition to Failure or an Agent Merge/configuration change invalidates blocked-session derivations and updates title-bar/badge state synchronously; a newly matching cold session also starts its state snapshot asynchronously. These controls are not frame-rate input paths.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Acquire a session-state subscription when a session first enters the failing-CI classification path
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero on warm toggles; one per newly matching cold backend session, coalesced by backend resource.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: CI transitions recomputed blocking from existing GitHub state but did not subscribe to agent-host session state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Snapshot completion drives the eventual authoritative classification but is asynchronous; transport/restoration load is concurrent with the UI update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N merged sessions for each blocked-list recomputation; F currently failing sessions contribute Agent Merge dependencies. A single session toggle normally changes one dependency, while a global setting can affect all F.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Warm Agent Merge/config reads are local observables. Newly failing cold sessions start one subscription each; if multiple CI models transition together, subscriptions are unbounded across those distinct sessions. Multiple BlockedSessions instances share the provider's one subscription per session.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm provider/configuration observables reuse cached values. CI/PR model references remain shared. Leaving Failure removes the Agent Merge dependency; after the last observer leaves, the provider schedules wire release after 30 seconds. While Failure persists, repeated updates do not create another subscription for the same session.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for subscription acquisition and dependency invalidation; lower for any user-visible synchronous recomputation cost beyond the already reported boundary mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Global setting changes are infrequent and observable transaction coalescing may reduce downstream recomputation, so no separate CPU finding is warranted. Bursts from multiple simultaneous CI transitions depend on polling timing.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported per-session subscription fan-out. No additional independent performance finding: warm changes use cached local observables, and the remaining full-list recomputation occurs on relatively infrequent control/status events.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Traced blocked-session consumers, observable lifecycles, GitHub model caching, provider state ownership, protocol subscription transport, concurrency, and cleanup. Submitted one medium-severity finding for diff-introduced per-session agent-host subscription fan-out and retained session state; no regression-fix learning signal applies.
